notes:
Vermont's recurring entity-level levy on a default LLC is the $250 minimum tax of 32 V.S.A. § 5921: a partnership-taxed limited liability company subject to § 5920 'shall pay an annual tax of $250.00 to the Commissioner of Taxes on or before the due date prescribed for the filing of the entity's federal return'. The Department of Taxes administers it through the Business Entity Income Tax return (BI-471 or BI-476) and calls it 'the Business Entity Income Tax, also known as the $250 minimum tax'. basis is flat: the $250 figure does not scale with any measure of the LLC's activity. The due date is the federal return due date (for calendar-year entities, March 15 / the next business day; the collector's 2026 calendar prints March 16). firstYearExemption is false: the statute states no first-year waiver, and the only exemption is the narrow class of partnerships limited to maintaining intangible investments with annual investment income not over $5,000 and total assets not over $20,000 - an entity class, not a first-year rule.
collectedWithAnnualReport is false: root states.json carries annual_report_fee 45 for Vermont, the Secretary of State's annual report fee, a separate payment with no tax to overlap. The minimum tax is paid to the Commissioner of Taxes with the Business Entity Income Tax return.
Two other Vermont franchise-type taxes are excluded from this record. The corporate income tax's minimum (32 V.S.A. § 5832, receipts-scaled $100 to $100,000) applies to active corporations, and the Department's own corporate page says LLCs electing C treatment are the only LLCs it reaches. The digital business entity franchise tax of § 5832a applies only to business entities that qualify as and elect digital business entity status, and its measures (authorized capital stock) are corporate measures, not a default LLC's.
stateIncomeTax: members owe Vermont personal income tax on their pass-through shares; the Department's own page says LLC income 'passes through to the shareholders, partners, or members and is taxed at the individual or corporate income tax rate'. The 2025 rate schedule tops out at 8.75% on every filing status. Vermont's only entity-level payment election is the composite return of 32 V.S.A. § 5920(b) - the Commissioner may permit a partnership or LLC to file composite returns and make composite payments on behalf of some or all of its NONRESIDENT partners or members; resident owners file their own returns. That is why hasPTETElection is true with this scope spelled out: it is a genuine entity-level election, but not a full pass-through entity tax covering resident owners.
